clue.text: Anger at nasty smell from plant

parts.note: BO is body odour, a nasty smell
anger means rage

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at a foul smell coming off a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger at' reads like the start of a sentence about a mood, but anger is just a piece and the plant comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a herb with blue star-shaped flowers, so it is a garden plant.

clue.text: What could be outside room at end of spout?

definitions.text: What could be outside room at end of spout?

parts.note: in Scots 'but and ben', the but is the outer room of a two-roomed cottage

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A riddle about something at the end of a spout, outside a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is the Scots word for the outer room of a cottage (the ben is the inner one). The whole clue also describes a rainwater cask set at the foot of a downpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A water butt is a large cask standing outdoors to catch rainwater from a downpipe.

clue.text: Runs coming with one big hit more likely to get you caught out

definitions.text: more likely to get you caught out

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral for one
in cricket a skier is a shot hit very high, easily caught

explanation.surface: A cricket observation: going for runs with one big shot makes a batsman likelier to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: A skier in cricket is a ball hit high in the air, which gives fielders time to catch it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something riskier carries more danger, so it is more likely to catch you out.

clue.text: Black stuff in earth pig turned over

indicators.note: turned over, as soil is dug, signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram

explanation.surface: A pig rooting in the soil turns up some black material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' rearranges EARTH PIG into the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite is a black form of carbon used in pencil leads.

clue.text: Lovely Carol eating potatoes

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
mash is mashed potatoes

explanation.surface: Carol, a woman, is tucking into some potatoes, which is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb meaning sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British for excellent, wonderful or lovely.

clue.text: Girl in limbo lashing out irresponsibly

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
something in limbo is undecided, pending

explanation.surface: An undecided girl is splashing money about.
explanation.walkthrough: To lash out is British for spending freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspending is wasting money, which is what lashing out irresponsibly means.

clue.text: Sledge in slide, going over over over!

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece going over others is placed above them

parts.note: a skid is a slide
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
O again for over

explanation.surface: A sledge sliding along goes right over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'over' belongs to 'going over', placing SKID above the two Os that the next two 'over's give.
explanation.definitionFit: A Skidoo is a motorised snow sledge, a trade name now used generally.

clue.text: Grandma dumped in one city without any thought

indicators.note: dumped in means put inside something else

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
nan is a British word for grandma

explanation.surface: Grandma has been abandoned somewhere in a city without a second thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city, very common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something inanely is doing it stupidly, with no thought behind it.

clue.text: Fine fellow with items to sell on the harbour

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: goods are merchandise, items for sale
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A man selling his wares down at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sport is a decent, generous person who takes things well.

clue.text: Italian territory to which American and Canadian go

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for territory
US means American
Can is an abbreviation for Canadian

explanation.surface: North Americans travelling to a region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan describes something from Tuscany, a region of Italy, so it is an Italian adjective.

clue.text: Lost in a tower, some characters found passage reappearing

indicators.note: some characters says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a tower keeps finding the same passage.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'characters found passage reappearing' as the definition; 'some characters' is the hidden-word signal, 'found' a link, and 'passage reappearing' defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a musical phrase that keeps repeating throughout a piece.

clue.text: Piece of cartilage given six chops — dire op bungled?

indicators.note: a bungled job is botched, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram

explanation.surface: A surgeon hacks away six times at someone in a disastrous operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' rearranges all of SIX CHOPS DIRE OP; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The xiphoid process is the small piece of cartilage at the lower end of the breastbone.

clue.text: Nice walk I'd arranged on unknown Roman road

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the next
arranged signals that these words' letters are reordered

parts.note: used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram, the apostrophe ignored
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone planned a nice walk along an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NICE WALK I'D, and Y comes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Icknield Way is an ancient track across southern England, used by the Romans.

clue.text: Mark on script by a man in charge looking after things

parts.note: a caret is a proofreading mark showing where to insert text
a king is a man who rules

explanation.surface: A man in charge leaves a mark on a written script.
explanation.definitionFit: Caretaking is looking after a building or property on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Company chap accepting first indications from the accountants — normal ratio

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gent is a chap

indicators.note: the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for normal

explanation.surface: A firm's employee takes the first hints from the accountants about a normal ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the container; 'normal' looks like part of the definition but gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotangent is a trigonometric ratio of a right-angled triangle's sides.

clue.text: One may be seen as "old" after end of first year!

definitions.text: One may be seen as "old" after end of first year!

indicators.note: after places the last piece behind the others
end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A first-year student may feel seasoned once that year ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a beginner who has finished a first year might call themselves 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a novice or beginner, like someone in their first year.

clue.text: Coach wants bit of commitment, not bit of moaning, in match

indicators.note: not marks one letter swapped out for another

parts.note: a match is a marriage

indicators.note: a bit here is the first letter of the word
again the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A coach wants commitment, not complaining, during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In MARRIAGE, the M ('bit of moaning') is replaced by C ('bit of commitment').
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a railway coach or horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: Book that's recalled in English test

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A book remembered in an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns E MOT round; the MOT is the yearly safety test for cars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, especially a large heavy one.

clue.text: Fellow with gold round fringes of the cloak

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the fringes are the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man in gold trim wears the cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteau is a loose cloak or gown, from the French for coat.

clue.text: Note a register with hardly any notes?

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a register is a list

explanation.surface: A musical note and a register for a piece with very few notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with hardly any notes' describes minimalist music, built from very few repeated notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalist means using the bare minimum of elements, such as few musical notes.

clue.text: One makes atmosphere, charged with excitement, noisier!

indicators.note: excitement agitates the letters into a new order

parts.note: used as written in the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone makes the atmosphere charged and louder with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' belongs to the definition, about electrically charged air; 'with excitement' rearranges NOISIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ioniser is a device that electrically charges the air in a room.

clue.text: Cell's nucleus lacking in particle

indicators.note: nucleus lacking means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: a neutron is a subatomic particle

explanation.surface: A biological cell lacks a nucleus inside a particle.
explanation.walkthrough: The nucleus is the central letter, T, of NEUTRON; 'Cell's' reads as 'Cell is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell.

clue.text: One rebelling is transformed by books of Bible, becoming peaceful

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: used as written in the anagram
used as written in the anagram
NT is the New Testament, a collection of the Bible's books

explanation.surface: A rebel is converted by reading scripture and becomes peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is transformed' rearranges ONE REBELLING; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonbelligerent means not taking part in war or aggression, so peaceful.

clue.text: Lump hard to get out of fabric

indicators.note: get out of means leave, so the letter is removed

parts.note: cloth is fabric
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hard lump is difficult to remove from fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard' looks like 'difficult' but gives H, which 'to get out of' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a lump, as of blood or cream.

clue.text: One may be surprised when they go up — must be hairy!

definitions.text: One may be surprised when they go up — must be hairy!

parts.words: One may be surprised when they go up — must be hairy!
parts.note: a person shows surprise by raising the hairy arches above the eyes

explanation.surface: Something hairy goes up whenever someone is surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: People raise their eyebrows in surprise, and eyebrows are strips of hair.

clue.text: Against having a girl around as a slave

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone opposes keeping a girl as a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the girl backwards; 'as a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal subordinate, and loosely a servant or slave.

clue.text: Contests organised by general in one of his towns?

indicators.note: the general is placed in the town, so 'in' puts one word inside the other

parts.note: Tours is a French town, so one of a French general's towns
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Competitions staged by a general in a town he commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised by' is a link. The question mark admits Ney was a marshal rather than a general and that Tours is his only in being French.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourneys are tournaments, contests between knights or competitors.

clue.text: On the street catch the sound of old newspaperman

parts.note: to hear is to catch the sound of something
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone on the street overhears an old newspaper man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch the sound of' just means hear; nothing here is a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst was a famous American newspaper publisher.
